chunks: 5307 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abu Wallad, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah عليه السلام about a man who was killed and had young and adult children. I said: What do you think if his adult children pardon?

He عليه السلام said: “He is not to be killed, and the pardon of the adults is valid regarding their shares. Then when the minors become adults, they have the right to seek their share from the blood money.”
And it has also been narrated: “If one of the heirs pardons concerning the blood, retaliation is lifted.”

key_terms.الدَّمِ: the blood claim arising from unlawful killing
key_terms.الدِّيَةِ: blood money paid as compensation for killing
key_terms.الْأَوْلِيَاءِ: the legal heirs or claimants entitled to the blood claim
key_terms.حِصَصِهِمْ: their individual legal shares in the claim
key_terms.عَفْوُ الْكِبَارِ: the pardon granted by the adult heirs

ai.seo_question: What happens in Islamic law if some heirs of a murder victim pardon while others are minors?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning qiṣāṣ when the heirs of a murdered person include both adults and minors. The adult heirs may pardon only with respect to their own shares, and the minors retain their right to claim their portion of the diyah once they reach adulthood; it is also reported that if one of the heirs pardons the blood, qiṣāṣ is lifted.
